4:1.sourceText: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος, πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.
4:1.targetText: Then Jesus was led up to the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tempted by the Devil,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Jesus has no separately expressed English word.

4:2.sourceText: καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ τεσσεράκοντα νύκτας ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν.
4:2.targetText: and having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward He hungered.

4:3.sourceText: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται.
4:3.targetText: And the tempting [one], having come to Him, said, “If You are the Son of God—speak that these stones may become loaves.”

groups.note: The actual Greek article makes tempting a substantival description, the tempting one. English one is nominal support for that article/participle construction, not a separately printed Greek numeral; its brackets do not make the actual nominal relation absent.
The actual dative Him marks the addressee of said. LSV places to Him after having come; the same approached/addressee participant is retained with that attachment difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with these stones.

4:4.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Γέγραπται Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος Θεοῦ.
4:4.targetText: But He answering said, “It has been written: Man does not live on bread alone, but on every word coming forth from the mouth of God.”

groups.note: Pinned Greek has future will live, ζήσεται; LSV expresses the general rule with present does ... live. The actual living predicate remains linked with that tense wording explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with generic Man has no separately expressed English word.

4:5.sourceText: Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ,
4:5.targetText: Then the Devil takes Him to the [holy] city, and sets Him on the pinnacle of the temple,

groups.note: Holy is actually written in N1904, ἁγίαν, despite the English editorial brackets. It retains its real Greek adjective counterpart.
The Greek aorist set/placed predicate ἔστησεν is rendered historical-present sets in LSV. The same placement head remains linked with the tense difference explicit.

4:6.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε, μή ποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
4:6.targetText: and says to Him, “If You are the Son of God—cast Yourself down, for it has been written that, His messengers He will charge concerning you, and on hands they will bear you up, that you may not dash your foot on a stone.”

groups.note: The actual μήποτε negative-purpose expression means lest/so that not; English distributes its force as that ... not. The whole construction is retained without claiming the temporal/indefinite component independently means that.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His messengers.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with your foot.

4:7.sourceText: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πάλιν γέγραπται Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου.
4:7.targetText: Jesus said to him again, “It has been written: You will not tempt the LORD your God.”

groups.note: The Greek article introduces God in the appositional Lord-God title; English places its one definite article before LORD in the LORD your God. The same definite Lord/God referent is retained with that article-position change explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Jesus has no separately expressed English word.

4:8.sourceText: Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν, καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν,
4:8.targetText: Again the Devil takes Him to a very high mountain, and shows to Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their glory.

4:9.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω, ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι.
4:9.targetText: and says to Him, “All these I will give to You, if falling down You may worship me.”

groups.note: N1904 writes past said, εἶπεν; LSV uses historical-present says. The actual saying predicate is retained with its tense wording difference explicit.

4:10.sourceText: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὕπαγε, Σατανᾶ· γέγραπται γάρ Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
4:10.targetText: Then Jesus says to him, “Go—Satan, for it has been written: You will worship the LORD your God, and Him only will you serve.”

groups.note: The actual Greek article introduces God in the appositional Lord-God title; English places the one definite article before LORD. Its same definite referent remains paired despite the title phrase reordering.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Jesus has no separately expressed English word.

4:11.sourceText: Τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
4:11.targetText: Then the Devil leaves Him, and behold, messengers came and were ministering to Him.

4:12.sourceText: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάνης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
4:12.targetText: And Jesus, having heard that John was delivered up, withdrew to Galilee,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Galilee has no separately expressed English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names Jesus as the withdrawing subject; N1904 has the implicit subject of the hearing/withdrawing predicates without a written Jesus name here.

4:13.sourceText: καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλείμ·
4:13.targetText: and having left Nazareth, having come, He dwelt at Capernaum that is by the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali,

groups.note: N1904 uses the Nazara name form Ναζαρά, while LSV prints Nazareth. These are documented forms of the same locality, preserving the actual Greek proper-name form without relabeling its text.

The actual attributive seaside adjective παραθαλασσίαν is rendered by the sea. The relative-clause copula is is English support with no written Greek be verb and is explained separately; sea is an expansion of the actual adjective, not an independent Greek sea noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Nazara/Nazareth has no separately expressed English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative-clause copula for the actual attributive adjective; no corresponding Greek be verb is written at this occurrence.

4:14.sourceText: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος
4:14.targetText: that it might be fulfilled that was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

4:15.sourceText: Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλείμ, ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν,
4:15.targetText: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations!

4:16.sourceText: ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα, καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς.
4:16.targetText: The people that is sitting in darkness saw a great light, and to those sitting in a region and shadow of death—light arose to them.”

4:17.sourceText: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς κηρύσσειν καὶ λέγειν Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
4:17.targetText: From that time Jesus began to proclaim and to say, “Convert, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near.”

groups.note: The actual then adverb τότε is expressed as that time after From; the English time noun is temporal support for the same actual adverb, not an independently printed Greek time noun.
The actual repentance/change-of-mind imperative μετανοεῖτε is rendered Convert by LSV, preserving that original head without inventing a different Greek turning verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Jesus has no separately expressed English word.

4:18.sourceText: Περιπατῶν δὲ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν δύο ἀδελφούς, Σίμωνα τὸν λεγόμενον Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντας ἀμφίβληστρον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλεεῖς.
4:18.targetText: And Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Simon named Peter and his brother Andrew, casting a drag into the sea—for they were fishers—

groups.note: The actual cast-net noun ἀμφίβληστρον is rendered a drag in this fishing context. Drag names the net here; it is not an invented Greek dragging verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with the named-Peter modifier or his brother.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names the walking/seeing subject Jesus; N1904 has that subject implicit, without a written Jesus name at this point.

4:19.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς ἁλεεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
4:19.targetText: and He says to them, “Come after Me, and I will make you fishers of men,”

4:20.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
4:20.targetText: and they, immediately, having left the nets, followed Him.

4:21.sourceText: Καὶ προβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄλλους δύο ἀδελφούς, Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ Ζεβεδαίου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.
4:21.targetText: And having advanced from there, He saw two other brothers, James of Zebedee, and his brother John, in the boat with their father Zebedee, refitting their nets, and He called them,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with James of Zebedee or the possessive brother, father and nets phrases.

4:22.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὸ πλοῖον καὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
4:22.targetText: and they, immediately, having left the boat and their father, followed Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their father.

4:23.sourceText: Καὶ περιῆγεν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
4:23.targetText: And Jesus was going in all of Galilee teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people,

groups.note: The actual going-around imperfect περιῆγεν is rendered was going by LSV; the circuit/around nuance belongs to that compound verb rather than an omitted independent Greek around word.

Greek whole/all qualifies Galilee; English expresses this modifier as the partitive all of. Its of is support for that whole-region quantifier, not an independently printed Greek preposition or a genitive falsely added to Galilee.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with all of Galilee or their synagogues.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names Jesus at the circuit-going predicate; N1904 keeps the subject implicit without a written Jesus name in this verse.

4:24.sourceText: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν Συρίαν· καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις καὶ βασάνοις συνεχομένους, δαιμονιζομένους καὶ σεληνιαζομένους καὶ παραλυτικούς, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
4:24.targetText: and His fame went forth to all Syria, and they brought to Him all the ill having manifold oppressing diseases and torments—and demoniacs, and lunatics, and paralytics—and He healed them.

groups.note: Greek having badly is the actual idiom for being ill; the manner adverb and having participle jointly supply ill rather than isolated have = ill or badly = a whole sick person.

The actual Greek passive being held/afflicted by diseases and torments is recast as English having oppressing diseases and torments. Having and oppressing together express that affliction relation, with the passive-patient to active-condition wording explicit rather than a free having/oppressing lexical equation.

The actual σεληνιάζομαι participle designates the illness conventionally rendered lunatics in this historical text. The source keeps that written illness designation rather than a generic Greek insanity or moon noun substituted by the mapper.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles have no separately expressed English word with His fame or Syria.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds a conjunction before demoniacs; N1904 proceeds directly to the demoniac participle after the afflicted-conditions phrase without a καί there.

4:25.sourceText: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Δεκαπόλεως καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
4:25.targetText: And there followed Him many multitudes from Galilee, and Decapolis, and Jerusalem, and Judea, and beyond the Jordan.

groups.note: English there introduces the inverted followed-Him-many-multitudes construction; it belongs to that actual following predicate, not to a separately printed Greek location adverb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Galilee has no separately expressed English word.
